arxiv-2105-12183.title: Nonlinear Conversion of Orbital Angular Momentum States of Light Journal: oe Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2105-12183.creator: Pascal Bassène, \authormark 1,3,* Finn Buldt, \authormark 1,3 Nazifa Rumman, \authormark 2 Tianhong Wang, \authormark 1 Phillip Heitert, \authormark 1 and Moussa N’Gom \authormark 1
arxiv-2105-12183.description: Abstract We investigate the second harmonic generation of light field carrying orbital angular momentum in bulk χ ( 2 ) \chi^{(2)} material. We show that due to conservation of energy and momentum, the frequency doubled beam light has a modified spatial distribution and mode characteristics.

arxiv-2205-13486.title: Spike Variations for Stochastic Volterra Integral Equations
arxiv-2205-13486.creator: Tianxiao Wang, Jiongmin Yong
arxiv-2205-13486.description: Abstract Spike variation technique plays a crucial role in deriving Pontryagin’s type maximum principle of optimal controls for differential equations of several types, including ordinary differential equations (ODEs), partial differential equations (PDEs), and stochastic differentia equations (SDEs), when the control domains are not assumed to be convex. This technique also applies to (deterministic forward) Volterra intrgral equations (FVIEs).

arxiv-2302-12894.title: Multiple Imputation for Non-Monotone Missing Not at Random Binary Data using the No Self-Censoring Model
arxiv-2302-12894.creator: Boyu Ren, Stuart R. Lipsitz, Roger D. Weiss, Garrett M. Fitzmaurice
arxiv-2302-12894.description: Abstract Although approaches for handling missing data from longitudinal studies are well-developed when the patterns of missingness are monotone, fewer methods are available for non-monotone missingness. Moreover, the conventional missing at random (MAR) assumption—a natural benchmark for monotone missingness—does not model realistic beliefs about non-monotone missingness processes (Robins and Gill, 1997).

arxiv-2305-02548.title: Two-particle bound states on a lattice Journal: Annals of Physics
arxiv-2305-02548.creator: Pavel E. Kornilovitch
arxiv-2305-02548.description: Abstract Two-particle lattice states are important for physics of magnetism, superconducting oxides, and cold quantum gases. The quantum-mechanical lattice problem is exactly solvable for finite-range interaction potentials. A two-body Schrödinder equation can be reduced to a system of linear equations whose numbers scale with the number of interacting sites.

arxiv-2406-03679.title: On the Effects of Data Scale on UI Control Agents
arxiv-2406-03679.creator: Wei Li, William Bishop, Alice Li, Chris Rawles, Folawiyo Campbell-Ajala, Divya Tyamagundlu, Oriana Riva
arxiv-2406-03679.description: Abstract Autonomous agents that control user interfaces to accomplish human tasks are emerging. Leveraging LLMs to power such agents has been of special interest, but unless fine-tuned on human-collected task demonstrations, performance is still relatively low. In this work we study whether fine-tuning alone is a viable approach for building real-world UI control agents.

arxiv-2406-08832.title: Multiplexed Quantum Communication with Surface and Hypergraph Product Codes
arxiv-2406-08832.creator: Shin Nishio, Nicholas Connolly, Nicolò Lo Piparo, William John Munro, Thomas Rowan Scruby, Kae Nemoto
arxiv-2406-08832.description: Abstract Connecting multiple processors via quantum interconnect technologies could help overcome scalability issues in single-processor quantum computers. Transmission via these interconnects can be performed more efficiently using quantum multiplexing, where information is encoded in high-dimensional photonic degrees of freedom. We explore the effects of multiplexing on logical error rates in surface codes and hypergraph product codes.

arxiv-2411-07327.title: A finite-resources description of a measurement process and its implications for the “Wigner’s Friend” scenario
arxiv-2411-07327.creator: Fernando de Melo, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, Paola Concha Obando, Thiago R. de Oliveira, Raúl O. Vallejos
arxiv-2411-07327.description: Abstract Quantum mechanics started out as a theory to describe the smallest scales of energy in Nature. After a hundred years of development it is now routinely employed to describe, among others, quantum computers with thousands of qubits. This tremendous progress turns the debate of foundational questions into a technological imperative.

arxiv-2502-02246.title: Cosmic shear nulling as a geometrical cosmological probe: Methodology and sensitivity to cosmological parameters and systematics
arxiv-2502-02246.creator: David Touzeau, Francis Bernardeau, Karim Benabed, Sandrine Codis
arxiv-2502-02246.description: Abstract Tomographic weak lensing surveys contain intrinsic symmetries that depend solely on the geometric structure of the Universe. These symmetries can be revealed through null tests and verifying their validity provides constraints on cosmological parameters that govern the background evolution—particularly the redshift dependence of the angular diameter distance.

arxiv-2502-09360.title: Formal Integration of Electron Scattering Processes via Separation of Dynamical and Geometric Contributions
arxiv-2502-09360.creator: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Fabio Taddei, Vittorio Giovannetti
arxiv-2502-09360.description: Abstract By decoupling the geometric from the dynamical contributions in the scattering processes, we develop a method to compute the scattering matrix of electrons in a one-dimensional coherent conductor connected to two electrodes. In particular, we demonstrate that, in the high-energy regime, the transmission matrix converges to the Berry operator of the system.

arxiv-2504-17808.title: That Dot on the Screen: also, what about Born? And other objections to wavefunction physics.
arxiv-2504-17808.creator: W. David Wick
arxiv-2504-17808.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by W. David Wick. Abstract

In this paper I address the most common objections to the claim that Schrödinger was right in 1926:
the wavefunction provides the correct, and
complete
, description of atomic phenomena. I suggest that
the line of droplets in the Wilson cloud chamber, the click of the “photon detector”,
and “that dot on the screen” can all be explained within a context of wavefunction models and
Schrödinger’s-type equations, albeit nonlinear. No auxiliary hypotheses about point particles or probabilities are required.

arxiv-2510-16725.title: Local integral input-to-state stability for non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems
arxiv-2510-16725.creator: Yongchun Bi 1,2, Panyu Deng 2, Jun Zheng 2,3, Guchuan Zhu 3
arxiv-2510-16725.description: Abstract In this paper, we prove comparison principles for nonlinear differential equations with time-varying coefficients and develop Lyapunov analytical tools for the integral input-to-state stability (iISS) analysis of nonlinear non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems, which involve nonlinearities satisfying a superlinear growth, bringing difficulties to the iISS analysis.

arxiv-2511-12276.title: Reflections on the design, applications and implementations of the normative specification language eFLINT
arxiv-2511-12276.creator: L. Thomas van Binsbergen, Christopher A. Esterhuyse, Tim Müller
arxiv-2511-12276.description: Abstract Checking the compliance of software against laws, regulations and contracts is increasingly important and costly as the embedding of software into societal practices is getting more pervasive. Moreover, the digitalised services provided by governmental organisations and companies are governed by an increasing amount of laws and regulations, requiring highly adaptable compliance practices.

arxiv-2512-12882.title: Parity Nonconservation in Rb and Sr + due to Low-Mass Vector Boson
arxiv-2512-12882.creator: V. A. Dzuba, V. V. Flambaum, G. K. Vong
arxiv-2512-12882.description: Abstract We calculate the parity non-conserving (PNC) electric-dipole ( E ​ 1 E1 ) transition amplitudes for the 5 ​ s − 6 ​ s 5s-6s and 5 ​ s − 4 ​ d 3 / 2 5s-4d_{3/2} transitions in Rb and Sr + .

pmc-10649350.title: The Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio in Children with Bronchial Asthma
pmc-10649350.creator: Ewelina Wawryk-Gawda, Monika Żybowska, Klaudia Ostrowicz, Emmanuel Andrès, César Picado
pmc-10649350.description: The discovery of an effective airway inflammation marker which correctly identifies the condition and phenotype of asthma still constitutes a significant challenge. The determination of NLR, that is, the ratio of neutrophils to lymphocytes, would overcome this challenge. The role of the neutrophil–lymphocytic index in the diagnosis of specific types of asthma is investigated in the present study.

pmc-10704651.title: ‘Helper’ or ‘punisher’? A qualitative study exploring staff experiences of treating severe and complex eating disorder presentations in inpatient settings
pmc-10704651.creator: Sienna Bommen, Helen Nicholls, Jo Billings
pmc-10704651.description: BackgroundEating disorders have been described as challenging to treat, with the most severe cases requiring inpatient admission. Previous studies have explored staff’s perspectives on eating disorders and service provision. However, little is currently known about how staff experience working with severe and complex eating disorder presentations in inpatient settings and how they may be impacted by their work.

pmc-11459569.title: Foodborne Bacterial Pathogens in Animal, Food, and Environmental Samples Collected From the Physical Exposure of Children With Diarrhea in Ethiopia: A One Health Approach
pmc-11459569.creator: Tesfaye Gobena, Dinaol Belina, Ameha Kebede, Meseret Chimdessa, Abduleziz Jemal, Chafe Husen, Tine Hald
pmc-11459569.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Foodborne pathogens (FBPs) are transmitted principally through the consumption of contaminated food or drinking water and pose a remarkable public health risk, particularly in low-income countries. A cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2021 and January 2023 to estimate the prevalence, co-occurrence, and monthly patterns of FBPs in the physical exposures of children with diarrhea in Harar town and Kersa district, Ethiopia. Animal, food, and environmental samples were collected from direct or indirect contact sites of children with diarrhea.

pmc-12524833.title: Association of SGLT2 Inhibitors with Mortality and Bioprosthesis Valve Failure After TAVR: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study
pmc-12524833.creator: Olivier Morel, Amandine Granier, Lisa Lochon, Antonin Trimaille, Arnaud Bisson, Benjamin Marchandot, Anne Bernard, Laurent Fauchier
pmc-12524833.description: Highlights What is the clinical question being addressed? Can SGLT2 inhibitors improve clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), including reducing the risk of bioprosthetic valve failure? Key finding? In patients undergoing TAVR, the use of SGLT2 inhibitors was associated with lower risks of mortality and bioprosthetic valve failure.

pmc-12588707.title: Synergistic effect between cortical cerebral microinfarcts and brain atrophy on cognitive decline
pmc-12588707.creator: Jiannan Huang, Wei Ying Tan, Jiangbo Cui, Shin Hui On, Eddie Jun Yi Chong, Christopher Chen, Saima Hilal
pmc-12588707.description: Cortical cerebral microinfarcts are associated with brain atrophy in cross-sectional studies, with further investigation using longitudinal datasets being warranted. Moreover, little is known about their combined impact on cognition. This study aimed to establish the association between cortical cerebral microinfarcts and brain volume loss over time and explore whether they synergistically contribute to cognitive decline.

Importantly, ergosterol’s fungal origin offers a sustainable substitute for cholesterol, aligning with current trends in natural and vegan-friendly formulations. Methods: This study explored the effect of ergosterol content (10 mol% vs.

pmc-12661729.title: Variable steady inflammation and inflammatory responses in precision-cut lung slices from various IPF lung Regions
pmc-12661729.creator: Carlos Machahua, Thomas M Marti, Namrata Kewalramani, Patrick Dorn, Lavinia Neubert, Christina Petzold-Mügge, Manuela Funke-Chambour
pmc-12661729.description: BackgroundThe role of inflammation in the pathogenesis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains controversial. While immune activation is evident in IPF lungs, immunosuppressive therapies have historically been associated with adverse outcomes. Investigating the transcriptional response of IPF lung tissue to inflammatory stimuli may help elucidate the contribution of dysregulated inflammatory pathways to the underlying disease mechanism.

pmc-12800986.title: Bidirectional Tendon Strip: A Rectus Femoris Graft Harvesting Technique for Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
pmc-12800986.creator: Jia Ying Lee, Jun Wei Soong, Deborah Huang, Paul Chang, Ting Cong, Matthieu Ollivier, Zi Yang Chia
pmc-12800986.description: In recent years, alternative graft options for anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction have gained attention, with the quadriceps tendon and rectus femoris (RF) favored for their biomechanical robustness and biological integration potential. However, traditional retrograde techniques harvesting from the patellar insertion pose technical challenges.

pmc-13248545.title: One-Stage Revision for Low-Grade Periprosthetic Infection with Staphylococcus hominis Following Cruciate-Retaining Total Knee Arthroplasty: Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13248545.creator: Georgios Renieris, Natalia Renieri, Athanasios Georgokostas, Eleni Georgaki
pmc-13248545.description: Background:Low-grade periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) are diagnostically challenging and often present with subtle clinical and laboratory findings. The optimal surgical strategy – one-stage or two-stage revision – remains controversial.Case Report:We report a 74-year-old male with a low-grade PJI due to Staphylococcus hominis 6 months after cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty.

pmc-13481027.title: Marital Life after Infertility Diagnosis: Sexual and Intimacy Issues Experienced by Iranian Infertile Couples
pmc-13481027.creator: Ali Asghar Firouzian, Vajiheh Hazari, Ahmad Nasiri
pmc-13481027.description: Background:Infertility is a life-altering condition that not only affects reproductive capacity but also deeply disrupts emotional intimacy and marital stability in couples. Understanding couples’ experiences of changes in marital relationships following infertility can be valuable for healthcare providers’ care planning. This study aimed to explain the experiences of infertile couples regarding sexual issues and intimate relationships.

pmc-13532422.title: The High‐Sensitivity C‐Reactive Protein−Albumin−Lymphocyte Index Is a Prognostic Marker for All‐Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality in Patients With ST‐Elevation Myocardial Infarction
pmc-13532422.creator: Xinuo Ma, Wei Zhang, Ningli Zhang, Qinghua Zhong, Tao Shi, Sirui Yang, Fazhi Yang, Yujuan Peng, Lixing Chen
pmc-13532422.description: BackgroundInflammation and immune dysfunction may worsen the prognosis of patients with ST‐segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).AimsThis study aimed to assess whether the high‐sensitivity C‐reactive protein–albumin–lymphocyte index (hsCALLYI) could be used to predict the prognosis of STEMI patients who received emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) treatment.MethodsParticipants were categorized into three groups based on hsCALLYI tertiles.

pmc-13660576.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini feedback in scenario-based clinical reasoning among medical interns
pmc-13660576.creator: Hilal Hatice Ülkü, Fulya Torun, Selcen Öncü
pmc-13660576.description: SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:Artificial intelligence tools are increasingly used to provide individualized feedback in medical education. The aim of this study was to compare the quality of feedback generated by ChatGPT and Gemini during scenario-based clinical reasoning activities.METHODS:A convergent mixed-methods study was conducted with 32 medical interns randomly assigned to ChatGPT (n=16) or Gemini (n=16).
